Module io.github.brantunger.unruly.core
Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api

Class RuleSetInfo

java.lang.Object
io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RuleSetInfo
public final class RuleSetInfo extends Object
The rules an engine has loaded, from RulesEngine.rules(): the rules themselves, a checksum that identifies them, and when they were loaded. An audit can record the checksum with a decision, and compare it later with the rules a run used (RunResult.ruleSetChecksum()).

Before the first successful RulesEngine.load(List), the engine's rules() has no rules, the checksum of an empty rule list, and a null load time. A run started before a reload finishes with the rules it started with, so its RunResult.ruleSetChecksum() can differ from the checksum() the engine reports afterwards.

It's a final class rather than a record, so a later 2.x release can add accessors without breaking code compiled against this one.

      Creates the information about a loaded rule list. The engine creates its own; this is for a class that implements RulesEngine, such as a decorator or a test double.
      Parameters:
      rules - The rules, in evaluation order; copied
      checksum - Their checksum, as checksum() describes it
      loadedAt - When they were loaded, or null if no rules have been loaded
      Returns:

    • checksum

      public String checksum()
      Returns a checksum that identifies the loaded rules, so a decision can be tied to a version of them.

      It's the lowercase hex SHA-256 of every rule in evaluation order. Each rule contributes, in this order: its name; its priority as decimal text; the expression language as the engine resolved it (so a rule with no language contributes the engine's default language); its condition; its action; true or false for whether it's enabled; its validFrom and validTo as ISO-8601 text in UTC, as Instant.toString() writes them, such as 2027-06-01T00:00:00Z; and its tags. Each value is written as its length in bytes, as four bytes most significant first, followed by its UTF-8 bytes; a null priority, validFrom or validTo is written as the length -1. The tags are written as how many there are, as four bytes, followed by each tag as a value, in the order of their UTF-8 bytes compared as unsigned numbers. A rule's description isn't included, because it doesn't affect what the rules do, so editing it doesn't change the checksum. Another system can compute the same value from the same rules.

      Returns:
      The checksum; for an empty rule list, the SHA-256 of no bytes
